description: We are a team of students passionate about space, engineering, AI, software, and innovation. Our interests include aerospace, AI/ML, coding, web development, hardware, data analysis, and design. We are looking for motivated members with creative ideas, technical skills, and problem-solving abilities. Curiosity, teamwork, and willingness to learn are highly valued. Join us and build something innovative together!
summary:
We developed ASTRA GUARD, a visual health self-check tool for astronauts on long missions. On the way to Mars, a message to Earth can take up to 22 minutes, so crews must be able to assess their own health.

Astronauts record readings from Bluetooth wearables, Arduino cabin sensors, the laptop camera or simple typed entries. ASTRA GUARD compares each value with that astronaut’s own normal and shows a clear colour: green, grey, yellow or orange. Each colour comes with a plain-language reason and a next step, such as checking again, resting, or reporting to flight surgeons. A clickable body map, live charts and daily reminders make it easy to use. A space-station game rewards healthy habits, never health numbers.

Doctors on Earth follow the whole crew from a Mission Control view, even on a phone. Reports and voice messages travel with realistic delays and wait safely during loss of signal.

ASTRA GUARD links NASA’s five spaceflight hazards to measurable signs, helping astronauts catch problems early and stay safe far from home.
details:
ASTRA GUARD is a health self-check and mission-support platform designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. When travelling to Mars, communication with Earth can take several minutes, so astronauts cannot always depend on immediate medical support. Our platform helps them monitor their health, understand changes and decide when to seek medical attention.

Astronauts can use their personal accounts to record health information through Bluetooth sensors, Arduino/ESP32 devices, laptop cameras and manual entries. The system compares new readings with each astronaut's personal baseline and uses simple colour-coded alerts to explain their health status. It also supports exercise monitoring, medication reminders, nutrition, sleep and wellbeing.

A separate Mission Control dashboard allows authorised doctors to monitor the crew, receive health reports and communicate through voice messages with simulated space communication delays. Messages are stored during communication blackouts and sent when the connection returns.

What makes ASTRA GUARD different is its combination of health monitoring, a clickable human-body interface, delayed mission communication, a space-station building game and Mission Bloom, a virtual garden inspired by plants grown on the ISS.

We use Python, Streamlit, JavaScript, SQLite, MediaPipe, Bluetooth technologies and Arduino/ESP32 sensors.

Our goal is simple: Help astronauts take better care of their health, recognise potential problems early and stay connected with medical teams, even when Earth is far away.

ASTRA GUARD is a prototype, not a certified medical device. It supports health awareness rather than replacing professional medical decisions.
